page: Microsoft Azure F8als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores without multithreading (1 thread per core). Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI are available.

Hardware allocations provide 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no local storage and no dedicated hardware GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 3080.89 in single-core stress-ng tests and 2106.0 in single-core Geekbench. Multi-core performance aligns with expected midrange metrics for an 8-core footprint, recording 24620.07 on stress-ng and 10749.0 on Geekbench.

Memory-intensive tasks reveal potential tradeoffs. Potentially uncached large-block read bandwidth tests at 37.09 GB/sec fall into the lower quartile, while cached small-block reads reach 1186.62 GB/sec. Text processing and lightweight LLM text generation perform strongly, yielding 310.16 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models. Medium model (7B) text generation achieves 8.93 tokens/sec. The instance is cost efficient for compute-bound pipelines that require dedicated physical execution threads and vector extensions without paying for unneeded memory capacity. Workload fit includes continuous integration builds, Clang compilation, web serving, batch encoding, and compute-focused microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure F8als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs on 8 physical cores powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture and running under Hyper-V, the instance includes AVX-512 vector support (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. It is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), no bundled local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark profiles show strong single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2106.0 and stress-ng score of 3080.89, alongside mid-range multi-threaded execution. Memory bandwidth on large uncached blocks is relatively constrained at 37.09 GB/sec. F8als_v6 provides resource efficiency for compute-centric workloads with moderate memory requirements, such as code compilation, CI/CD runners, batch processing, and high-throughput web serving.
